subject: SprintProof pilot: bridge vs bucket pricing decision
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@cloudlytics.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: CloudLytics Procurement <procure@cloudlytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SprintProof pilot - short runway and options

Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — SprintProof looks promising and the team is keen to push a small production sim in parallel with the pilot. Our current timebox runs out in 10 days and engineering needs another 3 weeks to validate throughput at 2M tokens/day.

Two questions from our side: can Redwood extend the pilot for 21 days and how would you prefer to structure the extension financially? Our procurement team prefers either a short "bridge" credit (apply to overage) or a small prepaid bucket at a discount. We also need clarity on whether additional engineering hours / SLAs can be included in the extension.

I've attached the SLA_requirements.pdf and the current_usage_report.csv so you can see our expected profile.

Can you please share options and numbers by EOD tomorrow? We need to finalize internally.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of ML Platforms
CloudLytics

Attachments: SLA_requirements.pdf (pdf), current_usage_report.csv (csv)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: (internal)
Date: 2026-06-13T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: FW: SprintProof pilot - short runway and options (need pricing + ops recs)

Karthik / David — forwarding CloudLytics' ask. Summary: 21-day extension, traffic profile ~2M tokens/day, they'd like either: 1) bridge credit to cover overage or 2) prepaid token bucket at a modest discount. They also asked about including eng hours / SLA bump.

Quick context: CloudLytics is in final eval and this is likely a $150k ARR conversion if we convert. They care about predictable cost during the sim. Their legal team is quick; procurement is on cc.

Please see the attached internal_calc.xlsx I started — it has rough token price bands and estimated engineering hours. Can you:
- Pick two clean commercial options (bridge credit amount + price, and bucket size + price)
- Recommend whether we should include 8 hours of eng support during the extension and if that should be billable or complimentary (they're strategic but we want to protect margin)
- Flag any legal/ops caveats (SLA changes, data retention requests)

I'm aiming to send external options tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Soojin
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

Attachments: internal_calc.xlsx (xlsx)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-14T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: SprintProof pilot - short runway and options (pricing thoughts)

Soojin — quick thoughts below, keeping numbers simple so procurement can run them quickly: 

Option A — Bridge credit (recommended for short runway):
- 21-day bridge credit of $12,000 applied to overage consumption
- Covers up to ~300k generated tokens (their profile suggests ~2M/day but we can cap generation portion they care about)
- No SLA change; standard pilot terms; engineering support: 4 hours complimentary, remainder billable at $250/hr
- Rationale: low friction, preserves sales agility, procurement-friendly since it looks like a credit line

Option B — Prepaid bucket (recommended if they want predictability):
- Prepay 500k tokens for $16,000 (effective ~3.2 cents / 1k tokens) — ~20% discount vs pay-as-you-go pilot rates
- Includes 8 hours of engineering support bundled (cover performance tuning and canary)
- SLAs: we can offer a 99.5% availability target for the extension window (no formal SLA amendment; operational commitment only)

Legal/ops notes:
- If procurement insists on an invoice/PO, use SprintProof_PO_template.docx (internal finance can fast-track).
- If they require audit logs / longer retention, highlight that private retention changes require a Private deployment addendum (longer lead time).

I'll defer to David on whether we should push for at least partial prepayment on Option A (e.g., 50% upfront).

-karthik
Sr. Pricing Manager

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@cloudlytics.com>
Cc: CloudLytics Procurement <procure@cloudlytics.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-15T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SprintProof pilot - short runway and options

Samir — thanks for the files and context. Per internal review we've got two options that should map cleanly to your procurement preferences. Short elevator summary below, full bullets after.

Option A — Quick bridge credit (low friction):
- 21-day bridge credit: $12,000 applied against overage/usage
- Estimated coverage: up to ~300k tokens (we’ll invoice any additional consumption at pilot PAYG rates)
- Support: 4 hours complimentary engineering support during the extension window; additional hours billed at $250/hr
- Billing & PO: we can issue invoice + credit line; no prepayment required

Option B — Prepaid predictability (best for cost certainty):
- Prepay bucket: 500k tokens for $16,000 (20% discount vs current pilot PAYG rate)
- Includes 8 hours engineering support for tuning + canary ramp
- Operational commitment: we’ll target 99.5% availability for extension window (operational SLA only)
- Billing & PO: we can accept PO and issue invoice; prepayment required to activate bucket

Recommended by Redwood: If CloudLytics needs the simplest path to extend quickly, choose Option A. If you want budget certainty and the extra eng hours, pick Option B. We can also do a hybrid (50% prepaid + smaller bridge) if that helps legal/process.

Next steps:
1) Tell me which option you prefer and whether procurement needs a PO or a DocuSign PO template.
2) If Option B, we’ll send a short amendment and the SprintProof_PO_template.docx for signature and request prepayment to activate.
3) If Option A, we’ll provision the credit immediately after a short purchase confirmation and schedule the 4-hour touchpoint.

I’m available for a quick 15-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the mechanics.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
